Trademark Search.shortDescription: Comprehensive search to identify existing trademarks and assess availability before filing.
Trademark Search.longDescription: A thorough trademark search across relevant classes and databases helps you understand conflict risks and avoid objections before committing to an application.
benefits: Saves cost of a rejected application

process.title: Database Search
process.description: Search Trademark Registry and related sources.

faqs.question: Is search mandatory before filing?
faqs.answer: No, but strongly recommended to reduce objection risk.

faqs.question: Does a clear search guarantee registration?
faqs.answer: No, but it significantly improves your chances.

faqs.question: How many classes should I search?
faqs.answer: All classes relevant to your current and near-future business activities.

Trademark Registration.shortDescription: Complete assistance with trademark application, filing, and registration for brand protection.
Trademark Registration.longDescription: We manage the entire trademark registration journey — from filing to responding to examination reports — to secure exclusive rights over your brand.

faqs.question: Can I use ™ before registration?
faqs.answer: Yes, once the application is filed.

faqs.question: What does ® signify?
faqs.answer: It denotes a registered trademark, usable only after registration.

faqs.question: How long is protection valid?
faqs.answer: 10 years, renewable indefinitely.

Trademark Renewal.shortDescription: Timely trademark renewal services to maintain registration validity and protect your brand.
Trademark Renewal.longDescription: Trademarks must be renewed every 10 years. We track deadlines and file renewal applications on time, avoiding lapse of your valuable brand rights.

faqs.question: When should renewal be filed?
faqs.answer: Within one year before expiry, though a grace period exists after.

faqs.question: What if renewal is missed entirely?
faqs.answer: The mark can be restored within a specified period with additional fees.

faqs.question: Is there a limit on renewals?
faqs.answer: No, a trademark can be renewed indefinitely every 10 years.

Trademark Objection Reply.shortDescription: Professional preparation and filing of responses to trademark objections raised during examination.
Trademark Objection Reply.longDescription: Examination objections must be addressed with strong legal and factual arguments. We draft a comprehensive reply supported by evidence and precedents.

faqs.question: What is the deadline to reply?
faqs.answer: Generally 30 days from receipt of the examination report.

faqs.question: What are common objection grounds?
faqs.answer: Similarity to existing marks or lack of distinctiveness.

faqs.question: What if the objection isn't overcome?
faqs.answer: A hearing may be scheduled, or the application may be refused.

Trademark Opposition.shortDescription: Assistance in filing or defending trademark opposition proceedings to protect your brand.
Trademark Opposition.longDescription: Whether opposing a conflicting application or defending your own, we prepare detailed opposition notices, counter-statements, and evidence for the proceeding.

process.title: Case Assessment
process.description: Review grounds for opposition or defense.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File notice of opposition or counter-statement.

process.title: Evidence & Hearing
process.description: Submit evidence and represent at hearings.

faqs.question: What is the time limit to oppose?
faqs.answer: 4 months from the date of advertisement in the Trademark Journal.

faqs.question: What happens if opposition is not defended?
faqs.answer: The application may be deemed abandoned.

faqs.question: How long do opposition proceedings take?
faqs.answer: They can take a year or more depending on evidence and hearings.

Trademark Hearing.shortDescription: Representation and preparation for trademark hearings before the Registry with supporting arguments.
Trademark Hearing.longDescription: When objections aren't resolved through written reply, a hearing is scheduled. We prepare submissions and represent your case before the hearing officer.

process.title: Preparation
process.description: Review case history and build arguments.

process.title: Representation
process.description: Attend and argue at the hearing.

faqs.question: Is a hearing mandatory?
faqs.answer: Only if the examiner isn't satisfied with the written reply.

faqs.question: Can hearings be attended virtually?
faqs.answer: Yes, video-conferencing hearings are commonly offered.

faqs.question: What happens after the hearing?
faqs.answer: The Registry issues an order accepting, refusing, or conditionally accepting the mark.

Trademark Assignment.shortDescription: Legal assistance for transferring trademark ownership through assignment agreements and Registry filings.
Trademark Assignment.longDescription: Trademark assignment transfers ownership rights to another party. We draft the assignment deed and complete the necessary Registry recordal.

faqs.question: Is Registry recordal mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, to reflect the new owner officially on public records.

faqs.question: Can a trademark be assigned with goodwill?
faqs.answer: Yes, assignment can be with or without the associated business goodwill.

faqs.question: Is stamp duty applicable?
faqs.answer: Yes, as per applicable state stamp duty rules.

Trademark Licensing.shortDescription: Drafting and registration support for trademark licensing agreements enabling authorized brand use.
Trademark Licensing.longDescription: Licensing allows third parties to use your trademark under defined terms. We draft the licensing agreement and manage registered user recordal with the Registry.

faqs.question: Is registered user recordal mandatory?
faqs.answer: It strengthens enforceability though not always legally mandatory.

faqs.question: Can I license my trademark exclusively?
faqs.answer: Yes, exclusive, non-exclusive, or sole licenses can be structured.

faqs.question: Who monitors quality under a license?
faqs.answer: The licensor typically retains quality-control rights in the agreement.

Trademark Rectification.shortDescription: Assistance with correcting, modifying, or challenging trademark records through rectification proceedings.
Trademark Rectification.longDescription: Rectification allows correction of errors in the register or removal of wrongly registered marks. We prepare and file rectification applications before the appropriate authority.

process.title: Proceedings
process.description: Present evidence and arguments as required.

faqs.question: What are common rectification grounds?
faqs.answer: Non-use, wrongful entry, or error in the register.

faqs.question: Who can file for rectification?
faqs.answer: Any aggrieved person, including competitors and the registered owner.

faqs.question: Is there a time limit for non-use rectification?
faqs.answer: Generally after 5 years and 3 months of continuous non-use.

Trademark Infringement.shortDescription: Legal assistance for addressing unauthorized trademark usage through notices and enforcement action.
Trademark Infringement.longDescription: When your trademark is used without authorization, we help enforce your rights through cease-and-desist notices, negotiations, or litigation as needed.

process.title: Notice/Negotiation
process.description: Send legal notice and attempt resolution.

process.title: Litigation, if needed
process.description: Pursue court action for continued infringement.

faqs.question: What remedies are available?
faqs.answer: Injunction, damages, and account of profits, among others.

faqs.question: Is a registered trademark required to sue?
faqs.answer: Registration strengthens the case, though passing-off action is available for unregistered marks.

faqs.question: How long does infringement litigation take?
faqs.answer: It varies significantly based on court and case complexity.

Copyright Registration.shortDescription: Assistance with copyright applications and registration to protect original creative works.
Copyright Registration.longDescription: Copyright registration provides documentary evidence of ownership for literary, artistic, musical, or software works. We manage application filing through certificate issuance.
requirements: Details of first publication, if any

process.title: Application Filing
process.description: Submit copyright application with work samples.

faqs.question: Is copyright registration mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, copyright exists automatically upon creation, but registration provides stronger evidence.

faqs.question: How long does copyright last?
faqs.answer: Generally the author's lifetime plus 60 years.

faqs.question: Can software be copyrighted?
faqs.answer: Yes, computer programs are protected as literary works.

Copyright Objection.shortDescription: Professional assistance in responding to objections raised during copyright registration proceedings.
Copyright Objection.longDescription: Objections during copyright examination require a clear, evidence-backed response. We prepare and file replies to keep your application on track.
benefits: Reduced delay in the registration process

process.title: Objection Review
process.description: Understand grounds raised by the examiner.

faqs.question: What are common objection grounds?
faqs.answer: Similarity to existing works or incomplete ownership documentation.

faqs.question: Is a hearing required for every objection?
faqs.answer: Not always; many objections are resolved through written replies.

faqs.question: What if the objection isn't resolved?
faqs.answer: The application may be refused, subject to further appeal options.

Copyright Infringement.shortDescription: Legal support against unauthorized copying, reproduction, or exploitation of copyrighted works.
Copyright Infringement.longDescription: We help enforce your copyright against unauthorized use through legal notices, takedown requests, and litigation support where necessary.
benefits: Protects creative and commercial value of your work

process.title: Notice/Takedown
process.description: Send legal notice or platform takedown request.

process.title: Litigation, if needed
process.description: Pursue court remedies for continued infringement.

faqs.question: What remedies exist for infringement?
faqs.answer: Injunction, damages, and account of profits, among others.

faqs.question: Can online content be taken down quickly?
faqs.answer: Yes, most platforms have takedown mechanisms for copyright complaints.

faqs.question: Is registration required to sue for infringement?
faqs.answer: No, copyright exists automatically, though registration aids evidence.

Copyright Assignment.shortDescription: Preparation and documentation of copyright assignment agreements for transferring ownership rights.
Copyright Assignment.longDescription: Copyright assignment transfers ownership of a work to another party, wholly or partially. We draft clear assignment agreements protecting both parties' interests.
benefits: Protects both assignor and assignee interests

process.title: Terms Discussion
process.description: Understand scope and terms of assignment.

faqs.question: Can copyright be partially assigned?
faqs.answer: Yes, specific rights like reproduction or distribution can be assigned separately.

faqs.question: Is registration required for assignment?
faqs.answer: Not mandatory, though registering the underlying work strengthens enforceability.

faqs.question: Can assignment be for a limited period?
faqs.answer: Yes, assignments can specify a defined term and territory.

Copyright Licensing.shortDescription: Drafting copyright licensing agreements allowing authorized use of protected creative works.
Copyright Licensing.longDescription: Licensing lets you monetize your work while retaining ownership. We draft agreements defining scope, royalty, and usage terms for licensed use.
benefits: Monetizes creative work while retaining ownership
requirements: Details of the work being licensed

process.title: Terms Discussion
process.description: Define licensing scope and royalty structure.

faqs.question: Is licensing exclusive or non-exclusive?
faqs.answer: Either, as negotiated and specified in the agreement.

faqs.question: Can a license be revoked?
faqs.answer: Yes, per terms specified for breach or expiry.

faqs.question: How is royalty typically structured?
faqs.answer: Flat fee, percentage of revenue, or a combination of both.

Patent Search.shortDescription: Detailed patentability and prior-art search to evaluate invention uniqueness before filing.
Patent Search.longDescription: A thorough prior-art search across patent databases identifies existing similar inventions, helping assess patentability before committing to the filing process.

faqs.question: Is patent search mandatory before filing?
faqs.answer: No, but highly recommended to assess patentability first.

faqs.question: What databases are searched?
faqs.answer: Indian, US, European, and international patent databases as relevant.

faqs.question: Does a clear search guarantee grant?
faqs.answer: No, but it significantly improves confidence before filing.

Patent Registration.shortDescription: End-to-end assistance for patent applications including drafting, filing, and prosecution.
Patent Registration.longDescription: We manage the complete patent process — drafting specifications, filing the application, and responding to examination reports — through to grant.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File the application with the Patent Office.

process.title: Examination & Grant
process.description: Respond to FER and secure grant.

faqs.question: What is the difference between provisional and complete filing?
faqs.answer: Provisional secures an early date; complete specification must follow within 12 months.

faqs.question: How long is patent protection valid?
faqs.answer: 20 years from the filing date, subject to renewal fees.

faqs.question: Can I request expedited examination?
faqs.answer: Yes, under specific categories like startups and small entities.

Patent Renewal.shortDescription: Timely payment and compliance assistance for patent renewal fees to maintain rights.
Patent Renewal.longDescription: Granted patents require annual renewal fees to stay in force. We track due dates and manage timely payment to prevent lapse of your patent.

process.title: Due-Date Check
process.description: Confirm the renewal fee due date.

faqs.question: When do renewal fees start?
faqs.answer: From the 3rd year onward, payable annually.

faqs.question: What if a renewal fee is missed?
faqs.answer: The patent lapses but can often be restored within a specified window.

faqs.question: Do renewal fees increase over time?
faqs.answer: Yes, fees generally increase as the patent term progresses.

Patent Objection Reply.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of responses to examination reports and Patent Office objections.
Patent Objection Reply.longDescription: First Examination Reports often raise objections on novelty, clarity, or prior art. We prepare detailed, technically sound responses to overcome them.

process.title: FER Analysis
process.description: Understand objections raised by the examiner.

faqs.question: What is the deadline to respond to FER?
faqs.answer: Typically 6 months, extendable by 3 months.

faqs.question: Can claims be amended in response?
faqs.answer: Yes, claims can be narrowed or clarified to overcome objections.

faqs.question: What if objections aren't resolved?
faqs.answer: A hearing may be scheduled before final decision.

Patent Hearing.shortDescription: Professional representation and preparation for patent hearings including technical submissions.
Patent Hearing.longDescription: When objections remain after written responses, a hearing before the Controller may be scheduled. We prepare technical arguments and represent your case.

process.title: Preparation
process.description: Review case and prepare technical arguments.

process.title: Representation
process.description: Attend and argue at the hearing.

faqs.question: Is a hearing mandatory?
faqs.answer: Only if objections remain unresolved after written responses.

faqs.question: Can hearings be attended virtually?
faqs.answer: Yes, video-conferencing is commonly available.

faqs.question: What follows the hearing?
faqs.answer: The Controller issues a decision to grant, refuse, or seek further clarification.

Patent Assignment.shortDescription: Legal documentation and filing assistance for transferring patent ownership between parties.
Patent Assignment.longDescription: Patent assignment transfers ownership rights formally. We draft the assignment deed and manage recordal with the Patent Office.
benefits: Legally valid transfer of patent rights

process.title: Recordal Filing
process.description: File for recordal with the Patent Office.

faqs.question: Is recordal mandatory after assignment?
faqs.answer: Yes, to update the official register and enforce rights as new owner.

faqs.question: Can a pending application be assigned?
faqs.answer: Yes, both pending applications and granted patents can be assigned.

faqs.question: Is stamp duty applicable?
faqs.answer: Yes, as per applicable state rules.

Patent Licensing.shortDescription: Drafting and advisory services for patent licensing enabling commercial exploitation.
Patent Licensing.longDescription: Licensing lets you commercialize your patent through third parties while retaining ownership. We draft agreements covering scope, royalty, and exclusivity.

process.title: Terms Discussion
process.description: Define scope, territory, and royalty terms.

faqs.question: Can a patent be licensed to multiple parties?
faqs.answer: Yes, under non-exclusive licensing arrangements.

faqs.question: What is a field-of-use restriction?
faqs.answer: Limiting the license to specific applications or industries.

faqs.question: Is compulsory licensing a concern?
faqs.answer: It applies only in specific public-interest circumstances defined by law.

Design Registration.shortDescription: Assistance with registering industrial designs to protect product appearance and configuration.
Design Registration.longDescription: Design registration protects the unique visual appearance of a product. We manage classification, application filing, and examination through to registration.

process.title: Classification
process.description: Classify design under applicable Locarno class.

process.title: Examination & Registration
process.description: Respond to queries and secure registration.

faqs.question: What qualifies as a registrable design?
faqs.answer: New and original visual features like shape, pattern, or ornamentation.

faqs.question: How long is design protection valid?
faqs.answer: 10 years, extendable by 5 more years.

faqs.question: Can functional features be protected?
faqs.answer: No, design protection covers only aesthetic, not functional, features.

Design Renewal.shortDescription: Timely renewal assistance for registered designs to maintain statutory protection.
Design Renewal.longDescription: Design registration requires renewal after the initial 10-year term to extend protection. We manage timely filing to avoid lapse of rights.

faqs.question: How long can design protection be extended?
faqs.answer: By an additional 5 years beyond the initial 10-year term.

faqs.question: What if renewal is missed?
faqs.answer: Restoration is possible within a specified period with extra fees.

faqs.question: Is protection extendable beyond 15 years?
faqs.answer: No, 15 years is the maximum total design protection period.

Design Infringement.shortDescription: Legal assistance for protecting registered designs against unauthorized copying or manufacturing.
Design Infringement.longDescription: We help enforce your registered design rights through legal notices, negotiations, and litigation against unauthorized replication.

process.title: Notice/Negotiation
process.description: Send legal notice and attempt resolution.

process.title: Litigation, if needed
process.description: Pursue court action for continued infringement.

faqs.question: What remedies are available?
faqs.answer: Injunction and damages for design infringement.

faqs.question: Is registration required to sue?
faqs.answer: Yes, unlike copyright, design protection generally requires registration.

faqs.question: Can minor variations avoid infringement?
faqs.answer: Depends on whether the overall visual impression remains substantially similar.

Geographical Indication Registration.shortDescription: Assistance with GI registration to protect products uniquely associated with specific regions.
Geographical Indication Registration.longDescription: Geographical Indication registration protects products whose qualities are linked to their geographic origin. We manage the application and evidence compilation process.

process.title: Examination & Registration
process.description: Respond to queries and secure registration.

faqs.question: Who can apply for GI registration?
faqs.answer: Associations, producers, or organizations representing the interested group.

faqs.question: Can an individual own a GI?
faqs.answer: No, GI rights are typically collective, not individual.

faqs.question: How long is GI protection valid?
faqs.answer: 10 years, renewable indefinitely.

Trade Secret Protection.shortDescription: Advisory and documentation services for protecting confidential business information and processes.
Trade Secret Protection.longDescription: Unlike registered IP, trade secrets rely on confidentiality measures. We help structure NDAs, internal policies, and documentation to protect sensitive business information.

process.title: Implementation Guidance
process.description: Advise on rollout and access controls.

faqs.question: Can trade secrets be registered?
faqs.answer: No, there's no registration system; protection relies on confidentiality measures.

faqs.question: How long does trade secret protection last?
faqs.answer: Indefinitely, as long as confidentiality is maintained.

faqs.question: What happens if a trade secret is leaked?
faqs.answer: Legal action can be pursued for breach of confidentiality or contract.

IP Due Diligence.shortDescription: Comprehensive intellectual property review to identify ownership, validity, and commercial value.
IP Due Diligence.longDescription: Before investments, acquisitions, or licensing deals, IP due diligence uncovers ownership gaps, validity risks, and infringement exposure across your IP portfolio.

process.title: Portfolio Review
process.description: Compile and verify all IP assets.

process.title: Risk Assessment
process.description: Assess validity, ownership, and infringement risk.

faqs.question: When is IP due diligence needed?
faqs.answer: Before M&A, investment, or major licensing transactions.

faqs.question: What does chain-of-title mean?
faqs.answer: The documented history of ownership transfers for an IP asset.

faqs.question: Can this review cover unregistered IP?
faqs.answer: Yes, including trade secrets and unregistered trademarks/copyrights.

IP Portfolio Management.shortDescription: Strategic management of intellectual property assets including registrations, renewals, and compliance.
IP Portfolio Management.longDescription: We provide ongoing management of your entire IP portfolio — tracking renewals, monitoring for infringement, and advising on new filings — as a single point of coordination.
requirements: Current IP management practices, if any

process.title: Portfolio Audit
process.description: Review existing IP assets and status.

faqs.question: What does portfolio management include?
faqs.answer: Renewal tracking, monitoring, licensing support, and strategic filing advice.

faqs.question: Is this suitable for small businesses?
faqs.answer: Yes, scalable engagement models suit businesses of any size.

faqs.question: How often is the portfolio reviewed?
faqs.answer: Continuously, with formal reviews typically conducted annually.

IP Legal Notice.shortDescription: Drafting and issuing legal notices concerning IP infringement, unauthorized usage, and disputes.
IP Legal Notice.longDescription: A well-drafted legal notice is often the first effective step against IP violations. We prepare and issue notices covering trademarks, copyrights, patents, or designs.
benefits: Formal, professional first step against violations

process.title: Evidence Review
process.description: Gather proof of the IP violation.

process.title: Notice Drafting
process.description: Draft the legal notice with demands.

faqs.question: Is a legal notice mandatory before suing?
faqs.answer: Not always legally required, but it's a recommended first step in most cases.

faqs.question: What if there's no response to the notice?
faqs.answer: Further legal action, including litigation, can be pursued.

faqs.question: Can a notice be sent internationally?
faqs.answer: Yes, though enforcement mechanisms vary by jurisdiction.
